# Free Proxy Health List

> 4,196 verified HTTP, HTTPS, SOCKS4 and SOCKS5 proxies across 117 countries, re-checked and republished every 30 minutes as TXT, JSON and CSV. No signup, no API key, no rate limit. https://xyzs996.github.io/free-proxy-health-list/

Every entry passed a protocol-correct handshake and an end-to-end relayed request before it was published; of a random 400-proxy sample of the published snapshot, 40.0% answered again on re-check. Most lists claim to be verified and publish no such number; this is that number, and it is deliberately not rounded up. Snapshot taken 2026-09-06T14:20:07Z. These are public proxies operated by unknown parties: never send credentials or personal data through one.

## Download

Stable paths that never move; a snapshot replaces the file in place.

- All proxies — 4,196 entries. TXT https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xyzs996/free-proxy-health-list/main/proxies/all/data.txt · JSON https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xyzs996/free-proxy-health-list/main/proxies/all/data.json · CSV https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xyzs996/free-proxy-health-list/main/proxies/all/data.csv · CDN https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/xyzs996/free-proxy-health-list@main/proxies/all/data.txt
- HTTP — 1,090 entries. Verified HTTP proxies for ordinary web requests — the widest client support of any proxy type, and no extra library to install. TXT https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xyzs996/free-proxy-health-list/main/proxies/protocols/http/data.txt · JSON https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xyzs996/free-proxy-health-list/main/proxies/protocols/http/data.json · CSV https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xyzs996/free-proxy-health-list/main/proxies/protocols/http/data.csv · CDN https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/xyzs996/free-proxy-health-list@main/proxies/protocols/http/data.txt
- HTTPS — 1,587 entries. HTTP proxies verified to open a CONNECT tunnel, so TLS traffic passes through end to end without the proxy reading it. TXT https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xyzs996/free-proxy-health-list/main/proxies/protocols/https/data.txt · JSON https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xyzs996/free-proxy-health-list/main/proxies/protocols/https/data.json · CSV https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xyzs996/free-proxy-health-list/main/proxies/protocols/https/data.csv · CDN https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/xyzs996/free-proxy-health-list@main/proxies/protocols/https/data.txt
- SOCKS4 — 930 entries. Lightweight tunnels that relay raw TCP for legacy tooling that predates SOCKS5. TXT https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xyzs996/free-proxy-health-list/main/proxies/protocols/socks4/data.txt · JSON https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xyzs996/free-proxy-health-list/main/proxies/protocols/socks4/data.json · CSV https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xyzs996/free-proxy-health-list/main/proxies/protocols/socks4/data.csv · CDN https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/xyzs996/free-proxy-health-list@main/proxies/protocols/socks4/data.txt
- SOCKS5 — 589 entries. The most capable proxy type: any TCP traffic, plus UDP and remote DNS so your resolver never sees the target. TXT https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xyzs996/free-proxy-health-list/main/proxies/protocols/socks5/data.txt · JSON https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xyzs996/free-proxy-health-list/main/proxies/protocols/socks5/data.json · CSV https://raw.githubusercontent.com/xyzs996/free-proxy-health-list/main/proxies/protocols/socks5/data.csv · CDN https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/xyzs996/free-proxy-health-list@main/proxies/protocols/socks5/data.txt

## What one record carries

`data.txt` holds one `host:port` per line, nothing else. `data.json` holds the health metadata behind every entry:

```json
{
  "proxy": "203.0.113.10:8080",
  "host": "203.0.113.10",
  "port": 8080,
  "protocol": "http",
  "latencyMs": 842,
  "qualityScore": 91,
  "checkType": "http_probe",
  "supportsHttps": true,
  "country": "US",
  "anonymity": "elite",
  "consecutiveSuccesses": 4,
  "reliabilityScore": 96.75,
  "reliabilitySamples": 41,
  "lastChecked": "2026-07-25T11:09:35Z"
}
```

`latencyMs` is the full round trip of a relayed request, not a TCP connect. `anonymity` is `elite` only when the origin address differed from the checker and no forwarding header was added. `lastChecked` is the moment that entry was proved, not the moment the file was written.

## Guides

Copy-paste recipes, each with a working command.

- [Free proxies for web scraping](https://xyzs996.github.io/free-proxy-health-list/use-cases/proxy-for-web-scraping.html): Rotate IP addresses across a scrape so a single address does not absorb every request and trip rate limits.
- [Python requests proxy setup](https://xyzs996.github.io/free-proxy-health-list/use-cases/python-requests-proxy.html): Use an HTTP or SOCKS5 proxy from Python's requests library.
- [Build a rotating proxy pool](https://xyzs996.github.io/free-proxy-health-list/use-cases/rotating-proxy.html): A working rotation loop with health tracking in about 20 lines.
- [Scrapy proxy middleware](https://xyzs996.github.io/free-proxy-health-list/use-cases/proxy-for-scrapy.html): Drop-in downloader middleware that rotates on every request and retries on failure.
- [curl proxy flags](https://xyzs996.github.io/free-proxy-health-list/use-cases/proxy-for-curl.html): Every curl proxy flag with a real command you can paste.

## Questions answered in full, with the figures behind them

- **How many free proxies actually work? Here is the measured rate, by protocol.** — the measured end-to-end success rate of a random sample, broken out by protocol, with the method and the timeout it was measured under. https://github.com/xyzs996/free-proxy-health-list/discussions/2
- **Where do I get a free proxy list by country, and how many are in each?** — the per-country file path, how many entries each country has in the current snapshot, and how thin the tail gets. https://github.com/xyzs996/free-proxy-health-list/discussions/3
- **How do I check whether a free proxy actually works?** — a working checker in ten lines, plus the four ways a naive check calls a dead proxy alive. https://github.com/xyzs996/free-proxy-health-list/discussions/4
- **Сколько бесплатных SOCKS5-прокси из этого списка реально работает?** — the same measured rates, the snapshot's per-protocol counts and the method behind them, written in Russian. https://github.com/xyzs996/free-proxy-health-list/discussions/5

## Boundary

Free public proxies are shared and operated by unknown parties. Never send passwords, tokens or personal data through them. Follow the GitHub Acceptable Use Policies: no spam, no attacks, no bypassing access controls, no scraping against site policies.

## Elsewhere

- [Repository](https://github.com/xyzs996/free-proxy-health-list): the files above live here; the checker that produces them and its publish schedule are in the README.
- [One-field form](https://github.com/xyzs996/free-proxy-health-list/issues/new?template=country.yml&came_from=llms.txt): which country did you need, and did this list have it? One word is a complete answer, the form asks for no evidence, and sourcing priority follows the answers.
- [API and filtering](https://xyzs996.github.io/free-proxy-health-list/api.html): what the public files answer, and what they do not.
- Same pages in [中文](https://xyzs996.github.io/free-proxy-health-list/zh/), [日本語](https://xyzs996.github.io/free-proxy-health-list/ja/), [한국어](https://xyzs996.github.io/free-proxy-health-list/ko/), [Español](https://xyzs996.github.io/free-proxy-health-list/es/), [Português](https://xyzs996.github.io/free-proxy-health-list/pt/), [Русский](https://xyzs996.github.io/free-proxy-health-list/ru/), [Türkçe](https://xyzs996.github.io/free-proxy-health-list/tr/), [Bahasa Indonesia](https://xyzs996.github.io/free-proxy-health-list/id/), [Tiếng Việt](https://xyzs996.github.io/free-proxy-health-list/vi/).

Sibling projects by the same maintainer, public data readable without an account:

- [Free LLM API](https://github.com/xyzs996/free-llm-api): permanent free tiers for language models, every published limit linked to the page it was read from.
- [AI coding field notes](https://github.com/xyzs996/llm-api-pricing): what AI coding agents actually cost, every figure kept with the sentence it was published in ([the table](https://xyzs996.github.io/llm-api-pricing/figures.html)).

Each of those publishes its own machine index in this same shape — one request, every address, each one dated. So does a fourth site by the same maintainer, which checks public IPTV channels:

- https://xyzs996.github.io/free-llm-api/llms.txt: which LLM APIs still have a free tier, and what the published limit is, each figure dated and linked to the page it was read from.
- https://xyzs996.github.io/llm-api-pricing/llms.txt: what an AI coding agent costs once a free tier ends: every figure kept with the sentence it was published in.
- https://xyzs996.github.io/iptv-doctor/llms.txt: which public IPTV channels answer right now, per country and per channel. No stream URL is published.
